The weights within the capstone are to be confirm.
:::

## What the capstone is

The capstone is **your own research project**: an existing or ongoing
analysis of yours, or one manageable part of it (for example one dataset and
the analysis behind one result). You apply to it what each lesson teaches. It
counts for **30%** of the course grade.

It is separate from the LTEE project: a different repository, your own data
and question. The LTEE project, which you build in the lessons, is assessed
on its own ([LTEE project](ltee-project.qmd), 40%).

## What you hand in

A GitHub repository with your project (set up in
[lesson 02](../pages/02-project-organization.qmd), with each lesson's tool
applied to it, up to [lesson 12](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd)), a
release of the version you hand in, and the reproduce report your partner
filed on it.

The repository can be **public or private**. If it is private, add the
instructor as a collaborator (and your partner, for the swap session in
lesson 12). A Zenodo DOI is not required for the capstone: if you want to try
the release steps on it, the
[Zenodo sandbox](https://sandbox.zenodo.org/) is fine. (The real Zenodo DOI
is required for the [LTEE project](ltee-project.qmd).)

## How it is assessed

Three sources of evidence, in this order:

1. **The *Reproduce* GitHub Action** on the released version: a fresh machine,
   a clean clone, `pixi install --locked`, `pixi run reproduce`. Green or red.
2. **Your partner's reproduce report** (the
   [template](reproduce-report-template.qmd)), from the swap session.
3. **The automatic checks** below, listed by the instructor's script
   (`pixi run check-capstone PATH` in the course repository), and a reading of
   the repository.

You can run 1 and 3 yourself at any time; there are no surprises. If your project did not start from the course
template, copy [`assessment/reproduce-workflow.yml`](https://github.com/khan-lab/cbio7501-f26/blob/main/assessment/reproduce-workflow.yml)
to `.github/workflows/reproduce.yml` in your repository.

## The rubric (100 points within the capstone)

| Area | Points | Full points when ... | Checked by |
|------|-------:|----------------------|------------|
| **Reproduces from a clean clone** | 25 | The *Reproduce* Action is green on the release; your partner reproduced the main result from the README alone. *Half points*: it runs after small fixes your partner could make from the error message. *None*: it does not run. | CI; reproduce report |
| **Project organization and data** | 15 | Template layout or an equivalent you can defend; raw data read-only and downloaded by a script with recorded sources and checksums; nothing generated or large in Git. | checker; reading |
| **Software environment** | 15 | `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock` committed and in sync (`--locked` passes); all tools come from the environment; platforms listed honestly (features where needed). Bonus: a container image built from the lock file. | CI; checker |
| **Automation** | 15 | One command (`pixi run reproduce`) runs everything, through Pixi tasks or a workflow (Snakemake or Nextflow); settings in a config file, not in code. | checker; reading |
| **Literate report** | 10 | A Quarto report (or notebook rendered with Quarto) in which every number, table and figure is computed when it renders; figures have captions and alt text; software versions shown. | reading |
| **Version control** | 10 | A history of small, described commits; work merged through pull requests; a tagged release. | GitHub history |
| **Documentation and openness** | 10 | README answers the seven questions; LICENSE (code) and stated licenses for text and data; valid `CITATION.cff`; data availability statement. No DOI needed (a Zenodo sandbox DOI is fine). | checker; reading |

## Levels, for each area

- **Full**: everything in the column, and you can explain each choice.
- **Partial** (about half): most items, or all items with one that a reader
  must guess or fix.
- **Insufficient** (none or few points): the area is missing or does not work.

The *Reproduces from a clean clone* area is the gate: a project that does not
run from a clean clone cannot get full points in *Automation* or *Software
environment* either, because nobody can check them.

## What is *not* assessed

- The size or novelty of the analysis. A small, honest analysis that anyone
  can rerun beats an impressive one that nobody can.
- Acceptance of anything by conda-forge, Bioconda or a journal ([S1](../pages/S1-packaging.qmd) is optional).
- Whether the repository is public, or archived on Zenodo: unpublished
  research can stay private, shared with the instructor.
- Sharing data you may not share: if your data is sensitive, use public or
  simulated data of the same shape for the reproducible version, and say so in
  the README.

## Self-check before you hand in

```{.bash}
# In a new folder, as your partner would:
git clone git@github.com:YOU/YOUR-PROJECT.git check && cd check
pixi install --locked
pixi run reproduce
pixi exec cffconvert --validate -i CITATION.cff
git tag            # your release tag is there
```

And from the course repository: `pixi run check-capstone ../check`.
